title: Backward Compatibility: Working with Legacy Code
text: Earlier versions (pre-v1.0 / pre-v0.1.0) MVBeliefUpdatr represented multidimensional category distributions, category templates, cognitive decision models nested tibble data frames list-columns vectors parameter matrices (mu, Sigma, m, S, etc.). convenient simple tabular wrangling, weakly typed tabular models suffered several limitations: Lack parameter dimension positive-definiteness validation object creation. Loosely coupled model metadata, cue labels, decision rules, noise parameters. Dispersed ad-hoc method dispatch across functions packages. Version 1.0 rebuilds MVBeliefUpdatr around R’s modern S7 object system, providing formal class definitions, robust property validators, unified generics, decoupled model family registry (MVBU_Family). provide smooth, non-breaking transition path existing analysis pipelines user scripts, MVBeliefUpdatr provides extensive compatibility bridge implemented R/S7--legacy-tibble-compatibility.R deprecation mappings.

what: 1. Motivation: Family Registration vs. First-Class Core Classes
title: Contributor Guide: Adding Permanent Model Families
text: MVBeliefUpdatr supports lightweight custom model families via new_mvbu_family() general MVBU_CategoryRepresentation instances, promoting frequently used foundational families core built-classes provides significant engineering advantages: IDE Tab Completion Discoverability: Dedicated constructor functions (new_uvg_category_representation() new_niw_category_representation()) feature explicit, typed arguments autocomplete seamlessly IDEs. Strict Property Validation Construction: Concrete S7 classes validate domain constraints immediately upon instantiation (e.g., positive variance, symmetric covariance matrices, probability distributions summing 1). High-Performance S7 Method Dispatch: Direct S7 class hierarchy dispatch avoids reflective introspection metadata property names runtime. Integration Compiled Stan Generative Models: Built-classes can interface directly precompiled Stan models C++ routines Bayesian parameter estimation.

title: Contributor Guide: Adding Permanent Model Families
text: Every built-model family adheres following structural conventions: Family Descriptors (MVBU_Family): Model families registered .build_builtin_families() within R/S7-class.R. family encapsulates: density_function: Pure mathematical density function supporting perceptual noise treatments ("no_noise", "sample", "marginalize"). sampling_function: Vectorized random number generator. expected_moments: Extraction first second moments (mu, Sigma). default_prior: Standard prior configuration constructor. stanmodel: Optional list specifying stanmodel_name (e.g., "NIX_ideal_adaptor") stanfit_class (e.g., "NIX_IdealAdaptorStanfit"), NULL Stan model associated. Internal Likelihood Closure Parity: Concrete category representation constructors handwrite custom closure math. Instead, instantiate S7 class uniformly derive category likelihood closure directly family descriptor: Base-Class-First Logic: Package methods algorithms target base class MVBU_CategoryRepresentation. Specialized methods implemented mathematical optimizations (Cholesky prefactorization) warrant concrete overrides.
code: rep <- MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation(...) rep@category_likelihood_function <- .make_family_likelihood_function(rep)

what: Step 1: Author S7 Class and Constructors (R/S7-class-{family}.R)
title: Contributor Guide: Adding Permanent Model Families
text: Create dedicated file R/S7-class-{family}.R containing: 1. S7 class definition inheriting MVBU_CategoryRepresentation. 2. S7 validator enforcing strict domain constraints. 3. Constructor new_{family}_category_representation() using .make_family_likelihood_function(rep). 4. Empirical constructor new_{family}_category_representation_from_data().
code: #' @rdname family-myfamily #' @export new_myfamily_category_representation <- function(   category_labels,   cue_labels,   param1,   param2,   metadata = list() ) {   # Rationale for retaining typed class constructor:   # Concrete typed constructors provide strict property validation, IDE tab   # completion, and fast S7 method dispatch, while obtaining the likelihood   # closure uniformly from the registered model family density function.   rep <- MyFamily_CategoryRepresentation(     category_likelihood_function = NULL,     metadata = set_labels(       metadata,       cue = as.character(cue_labels),       category = as.character(category_labels),       response_category = as.character(category_labels),       group = if (!is.null(metadata$group)) {         as.character(metadata$group)       } else {         character(0)       }     ),     param1 = as.numeric(param1),     param2 = as.numeric(param2)   )   rep@category_likelihood_function <- .make_family_likelihood_function(rep)   rep }

title: Contributor Guide: Extending MVBeliefUpdatr and Adding Model Families
text: MVBeliefUpdatr uses R’s S7 object-oriented programming system provide modular, strongly typed, extensible framework cognitive models speech perception categorization. model families MVBeliefUpdatr follow two-tier structural hierarchy:
code: MVBU_Object ├── MVBU_CategoryRepresentation │   ├── MVG_CategoryRepresentation     (Multivariate Gaussian) │   ├── UVG_CategoryRepresentation     (Univariate Gaussian) │   ├── MUVG_CategoryRepresentation    (Multiple Univariate Gaussians) │   ├── NIW_CategoryRepresentation     (Normal-Inverse-Wishart hyperprior) │   ├── NIX_CategoryRepresentation     (Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared hyperprior) │   ├── MNIX_CategoryRepresentation    (Multivariate NIX hyperprior) │   └── Exemplar_CategoryRepresentation(Non-parametric exemplar memory) └── MVBU_CognitiveModel     ├── MVG_IdealObserver             (Static multivariate observer)     ├── UVG_IdealObserver             (Static univariate observer)     ├── MUVG_IdealObserver            (Static multi-univariate observer)     ├── NIW_IdealAdaptor              (Dynamic NIW belief updater)     ├── NIX_IdealAdaptor              (Dynamic NIX belief updater)     ├── MNIX_IdealAdaptor             (Dynamic MNIX belief updater)     └── Exemplar_Model                (Non-parametric exemplar model)

title: Contributor Guide: Extending MVBeliefUpdatr and Adding Model Families
text: Ideal Observers represent perceptual agents fixed, known category distributions. evaluate likelihoods p(x∣c)p(x \mid c) directly category parameters (e.g., mean μ\mu covariance Σ\Sigma) form posterior beliefs p(c∣x)p(c \mid x) using Bayes’ rule. Ideal Adaptors represent perceptual agents uncertainty category parameters. maintain distributional beliefs (hyperpriors NIW, NIX, MNIX) incrementally update beliefs exposed novel perceptual evidence via update_template() Stan inference. Exemplar Models represent categories via collections stored exemplars evaluate category activations using perceptual distance metrics. downstream operations (posterior(), likelihood(), categorize(), evaluate_model()) dispatch polymorphically abstract base classes MVBU_CategoryRepresentation MVBU_CognitiveModel, new model family automatically inherits full workflow support soon implements core S7 method contract.

title: Contributor Guide: Extending MVBeliefUpdatr and Adding Model Families
text: single category representation stores category’s lower bound aa upper bound bb:
code: Uniform_CategoryRepresentation <- S7::new_class(   "Uniform_CategoryRepresentation",   parent = MVBU_CategoryRepresentation,   properties = list(     lower = S7::class_numeric,     upper = S7::class_numeric   ),   validator = function(self) {     if (length(self@lower) != 1L || length(self@upper) != 1L) {       return("lower and upper bounds must be single numeric scalars.")     }     if (self@lower >= self@upper) {       return("lower bound must be strictly less than upper bound.")     }     NULL   } )

title: Contributor Guide: Extending MVBeliefUpdatr and Adding Model Families
text: register Uniform family using register_model_family() new_mvbu_family(). provide closures likelihood evaluation, random observation sampling, expected moments:
code: uniform_family <- new_mvbu_family(   name_short = "Uniform",   name_long = "Uniform Bounded Category Observer",   name_details = list(     CategoryRepresentation_name = "Uniform_CategoryRepresentation",     CategoryTemplate_name = "Uniform_CategoryRepresentationTemplate",     CognitiveModel_name = "Uniform_IdealObserver",     CognitiveModelList_name = "Uniform_CognitiveModelList"   ),   density_function = function(x, rep, log = FALSE) {     stats::dunif(x, min = rep@lower, max = rep@upper, log = log)   },   sampling_function = function(rep, n = 1L, with_replacement = TRUE, ...) {     matrix(stats::runif(n, min = rep@lower, max = rep@upper), ncol = 1L)   },   expected_moments = function(rep) {     list(       mu = (rep@lower + rep@upper) / 2,       Sigma = matrix((rep@upper - rep@lower)^2 / 12, 1L, 1L),       weights = 1     )   } )  register_model_family(uniform_family)

what: 6. Contributing to Core: Why Promote Custom Families to Built-in Classes?
title: Contributor Guide: Extending MVBeliefUpdatr and Adding Model Families
text: lightweight family registration pattern (new_mvbu_family() + new_category_representation()) allows full runtime simulation, categorization, likelihood evaluation without defining new S7 classes, contributing family permanent built-class MVBeliefUpdatr core brings compelling engineering usability advantages: IDE Tab Completion Discoverability: Concrete typed constructors (new_uvg_category_representation() new_niw_category_representation()) expose explicit, named function arguments. Modern IDEs (RStudio, Positron, VS Code) provide instant tab completion parameters (e.g., mu, Sigma, kappa, nu), eliminating guesswork slot names. Strict Property Validation Object Construction: Dedicated S7 classes enforce mathematical domain constraints moment object creation (e.g., covariance matrices must positive-definite symmetric; degrees freedom ν>d−1\nu > d - 1; probabilities weights must sum 1). catches specification bugs early costly model fitting simulation loops run. Compile-Time Dispatch High-Performance Specialization: Core classes allow specialized S7 method implementations (Cholesky-factorized distance calculations analytical Stan priors) dispatch instantly without reflective inspection property names. Stan Generative Models C++ Compilation: Built-classes can couple directly compiled Stan models (.stan programs), enabling fast Bayesian parameter inference via MCMC variational inference unavailable arbitrary dynamic R closures. developed useful custom family wish contribute permanent built-class, consult companion developer guide: Contributor Guide: Adding Permanent Model Families.

Provide density_function, sampling_function, expected_moments, specify stanmodel list list(stanmodel_name = ..., stanfit_class = ...) (NULL Stan model exists). S7 Inheritance: specified, category representation inherits MVBU_CategoryRepresentation; cognitive model inherits MVBU_CognitiveModel. Method Coverage: dynamic, implement update_template() method new category representation type.

title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: MVBeliefUpdatr package provides Bayesian hierarchical Stan models incremental cognitive belief-updating speech perception multidimensional categorization experiments. models fit observer adaptor beliefs (e.g., Normal-Inverse-Wishart [NIW] Normal-Inverse-χ2\chi^2 [NIX]) across exposure blocks participant groups using MCMC sampling via rstan cmdstanr. Fitted models returned typed S7 objects inheriting MVBU_Stanfit (e.g., NIW_IdealAdaptorStanfit NIX_IdealAdaptorStanfit). vignette details: Preparing Data Inputs: Structuring exposure data bundling priors new_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input(). Model Fitting, Backends & Threading: Executing Bayesian estimation via fit_ideal_adaptor() fit_ideal_observer(), selecting rstan cmdstanr backends, configuring -chain (cores) within-chain (threads) parallelization. Model Summaries & Diagnostics: Printing, summarizing, evaluating convergence (rhat, neff_ratio, get_draws). Accelerated Post-Processing: Pre-extracting posterior latents closures add_posterior_latents() fast visualization. Model Comparison & Criteria: Storing information criteria add_criterion(), comparing models loo_compare(), generating posterior predictive checks pp_check().

title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: fitting model Stan, raw participant observations (containing continuous cue dimensions Formant frequencies F1,F2F_1, F_2 Voice Onset Time [VOT]) packaged alongside prior hyperparameters using new_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input(). input pipeline: 1. Standardizes scales continuous cue dimensions (e.g., z-scoring relative exposure distribution). 2. Sets conjugate prior distributions category parameters (e.g., mean m0m_0, scatter matrix S0S_0, prior sample size κ0\kappa_0, degrees freedom ν0\nu_0). 3. Creates strongly typed S7 input object based cognitive model family integration architecture: - NIW: NIW_IdealAdaptorStaninput (multivariate full covariance updating) - NIX: NIX_IdealAdaptorStaninput (single-cue univariate updating) - Early Integration (MNIX): {Integrator}_MNIX_IdealAdaptorStaninput (e.g., IdealIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptorStaninput, WeightedIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptorStaninput, CategoryWeightedIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptorStaninput, etc.; early projection z=𝐰T𝐱z = \mathbf{w}^T \mathbf{x} followed 1D updating) - Late Integration (MNIX): MNIX_IdealAdaptor_{Integrator}Staninput (e.g., MNIX_IdealAdaptor_IdealIntegratorStaninput, MNIX_IdealAdaptor_WeightedIntegratorStaninput, MNIX_IdealAdaptor_CategoryWeightedIntegratorStaninput, etc.; independent per-cue NIX distributions late decision-level weighting)
code: # Construct standard 2-cue NIW ideal adaptor Stanfit input stan_input <- example_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input(   model_family = "NIW",   n_cues = 2L,   seed = 42L )

title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: MVBeliefUpdatr supports two execution backends via backend argument: "rstan" (default): Fits models -process using rstan package. Precompiled models bundled package used directly, avoiding runtime C++ compilation delays. "cmdstanr": Fits models --process via cmdstanr interface CmdStan.

previous_headings: 3. Fitting Bayesian Models (fit_ideal_adaptor) > 3.2 Execution Backends: rstan vs. cmdstanr
title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: Speed & Toolchain: CmdStan provides access newer Stan versions (stanc3), faster C++ compilation, lower memory overhead long chains. Process Isolation: Running sampling separate command-line processes ensures MCMC errors crashes take active R session. Unified Object Architecture: Regardless backend, fit_ideal_adaptor() returns consistent S7 MVBU_Stanfit object whose @backend slot indicates backend used, whose @stanfit slot contains standard stanfit object. downstream functions (summary(), get_draws(), add_posterior_latents(), add_criterion(), pp_check()) work identically:
code: # Fitting via the cmdstanr backend fit_cmdstan <- fit_ideal_adaptor(   stan_input,   backend = "cmdstanr",   chains = 4,   iter = 2000,   warmup = 1000,   seed = 42 )  # Inspect the backend used fit_cmdstan@backend #> [1] "cmdstanr"

title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: MVBeliefUpdatr supports two complementary levels parallelization: -Chain Parallelism (cores): Runs multiple MCMC chains simultaneously across CPU cores. example, setting chains = 4, cores = 4 fits chain CPU core. Within-Chain Multithreading (threads): Divides computationally intensive likelihood loops across multiple CPU threads within single chain using C++ threading.

previous_headings: 3. Fitting Bayesian Models (fit_ideal_adaptor) > 3.3 Parallel Execution and Within-Chain Threading
title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text: threads argument can specified integer count list threads element: threads = 2 (threads = list(threads = 2)): Allocates 2 worker threads per chain. backend = "cmdstanr", model compiled stan_threads = TRUE executed threads_per_chain = 2. backend = "rstan", threads assigned via rstan::rstan_options(threads_per_chain = 2). Note Total CPU Cores: Total core allocation equals chains×threads\text{chains} \times \text{threads}. instance, running 4 chains 2 threads per chain requires 4×2=84 \times 2 = 8 available CPU cores.
code: # Parallel execution: 4 chains running across 4 cores, with 2 threads per chain # (8 cores total) fit_fast <- fit_ideal_adaptor(   stan_input,   backend = "cmdstanr",   chains = 4,   cores = 4,   threads = 2,   iter = 2000,   warmup = 1000,   seed = 42 )

what: Prior Hyperparameters vs. Truly Known Category Moments
title: Fitting and Working with MVBeliefUpdatr Stanfit Models
text:
MVBeliefUpdatr distinguishes prior hyperparameters (m_0, S_0, expected_Sigma_0) truly known category moments (mu_0, Sigma_0): Prior hyperparameters (m_0, S_0): Model observer’s prior belief exposure. exposure, category representations update via conjugate belief updating (NIW NIX), predictive likelihood Student-t. Truly known moments (mu_0, Sigma_0): Model categories whose mean vector covariance matrix fixed non-random physical constant. Fixing either moments determines conjugate belief updating predictive likelihood family: Case 1 (unknown): Standard NIW NIX conjugate updating; Student-t predictive likelihood. Case 2 (Sigma_0 known, mu_0 unknown): Category covariance fixed Σ0\Sigma_0. Category mean updated via Normal-mean updating (κn=κ0+n\kappa_n = \kappa_0 + n, μn=(κ0m0+nx‾)/κn\mu_n = (\kappa_0 m_0 + n  ar{x}) / \kappa_n). covariance known certainty, predictive likelihood reduces Normal distribution covariance (1+1/κn)Σ0(1 + 1/\kappa_n) \Sigma_0. Case 3 (mu_0 known, Sigma_0 unknown): Category mean fixed μ0\mu_0. Category covariance updated around known mean (νn=ν0+n
u_n = 
u_0 + n, Sn=S0+∑(xi−μ0)(xi−μ0)TS_n = S_0 + \sum (x_i - \mu_0)(x_i - \mu_0)^T). predictive likelihood Student-t νn
u_n degrees freedom. Case 4 (mu_0 Sigma_0 known): Category representation completely fixed. belief updating occurs exposure, predictive likelihood Normal(μ0\mu_0, Σ0\Sigma_0).
code: # Fix known covariance for /d/, estimate covariance for /t/ f_known_sigma <- fix_parameter(   value = matrix(c(100^2, 0, 0, 150^2), nrow = 2),   class = "Sigma_0",   category = "/d/",   cue_space = "original" )  # Fix known mean for /d/, estimate mean for /t/ f_known_mu <- fix_parameter(   value = c(F1 = 300, F2 = 1200),   class = "mu_0",   category = "/d/",   cue_space = "original" )  # Combine with global and prior specifications all_fixed <- c(f_global, f_known_sigma, f_known_mu)

text: Posterior draws can extracted tidy format using get_draws(). nest = TRUE specified, get_draws() provides draw-level expected covariance matrices (Sigma_exp), marginal covariance matrices (Sigma_marg), standard covariance matrices (Sigma). Standard MCMC convergence diagnostics (R̂\widehat{R} effective sample size ratio neff/Nn_{eff}/N) accessible via rhat() neff_ratio():
code: # Tidy posterior draws with draw-level covariance matrices draws_df <- get_draws(fit, nest = TRUE, summarize = FALSE) names(draws_df) #>  [1] ".chain"     ".iteration" ".draw"      "group"      "category"   #>  [6] "kappa"      "nu"         "m"          "S"          "lapse_rate" #> [11] "Sigma_exp"  "Sigma_marg"  # Convergence diagnostics across parameters head(rhat(fit)) #>   kappa_0_shared_param[1]      nu_0_shared_param[1] category_prior_param[1,1]  #>                 0.9903867                 0.9896015                 0.9610481  #> category_prior_param[1,2]     lapse_bias_param[1,1]     lapse_bias_param[1,2]  #>                 0.9610481                 0.9882127                 0.9882127 head(neff_ratio(fit)) #>   kappa_0_shared_param[1]      nu_0_shared_param[1] category_prior_param[1,1]  #>                 0.5272677                 0.7065037                 0.4123210  #> category_prior_param[1,2]     lapse_bias_param[1,1]     lapse_bias_param[1,2]  #>                 0.4123210                 0.5272677                 0.5272677

text: producing complex multi-panel category plots, categorization decision boundaries, posterior density curves across multiple exposure trials, downstream plotting evaluation routines frequently need access posterior latent parameter draws (m,S,κ,ν,𝚺exp,𝚺margm, S, \kappa, \nu, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{exp}}, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{marg}}) evaluate likelihood posterior functions across observation grids. default, extracting draws repeatedly MVBU_Stanfit object requires untransforming cue coordinates pivoting tables every call. Calling add_posterior_latents() extracts draw-level latents , computes expected marginal covariance moments, compiles vectorized evaluation closures, stores object’s @cache slot: parameters: Nested tibble containing draw-level representations m,S,κ,ν,𝚺exp,𝚺margm, S, \kappa, \nu, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{exp}}, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{marg}}, lapse rate across groups categories. likelihood_function: Closure evaluating category likelihoods arbitrary test observations across draws, returning 3D array [N_obs, K, N_draws]. posterior_function: Closure evaluating category posterior probabilities specified decision rules, noise treatments, lapse rates across draws, returning 3D array [N_obs, K, N_draws]. parameters: Point estimates category parameters aggregated across draws. expected_moments: Distribution summary (mean, SD, quantiles) category expected moments. marginal_moments: Distribution summary (mean, SD, quantiles) category marginal moments. likelihood_function: Closure evaluating category likelihoods directly marginal moments (returning 2D matrix [N_obs, K]). posterior_function: Closure evaluating category posterior probabilities directly marginal moments (returning 2D matrix [N_obs, K]).

text: fitting ideal adaptor model Stan, researchers often wish inspect beliefs evolve incrementally across exposure observations. reconstruct_update_history() generic takes MVBU_Stanfit object reconstructs sequential updating process MVBU_ModelList container: uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize" (default): Sequentially updates individual posterior MCMC draws (controlled ndraws, default 20L, optional parallelization via parallel = TRUE). Returns MVBU_ModelList holding lightweight MVBU_StanfitPosterior objects, faithfully capturing parameter estimation uncertainty across exposure checkpoints. uncertainty_treatment = "discard": Fast mode computes prior marginal moments sequentially updates single point-estimate ideal adaptor (e.g. NIW_IdealAdaptor NIX_IdealAdaptor) across step checkpoints (e.g. step_size = 10L). Returns MVBU_ModelList MVBU_CognitiveModel objects. list models results reconstruct_update_history() can used input model visualizations, s plot_categories plot_categorization_functions. See vignette “Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, Belief Updating” examples .
code: # 1. Fast point-estimate update sequence at checkpoints of 10 observations model_seq_fast <- reconstruct_update_history(fit, uncertainty_treatment = "discard", step_size = 10L) model_seq_fast #> <MVBU_ModelList>  # 2. Full posterior update sequence with parameter uncertainty (10 draws) model_seq_full <- reconstruct_update_history(fit, uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize", ndraws = 10L, step_size = 10L) model_seq_full #> <MVBU_ModelList>  # Inspect model labels along the exposure trajectory head(model_seq_fast@model_labels) #> [1] "N_0"  "N_10" "N_20"

what: 1. Introduction and The S7 Object Model
title: S7 Class Architecture, Constructors, and Workflows
text: MVBeliefUpdatr package provides computational cognitive models category representation, multidimensional perceptual decision making, Bayesian belief updating. Version 1.0 package redesigns underlying architecture around R’s new S7 object-oriented system (PEP / R Consortium object system). previous versions, category distributions cognitive models represented nested tibbles list-columns vectors matrices. accessible simple data-wrangling pipelines, weakly typed tabular models suffered several limitations: Parameter matrices dimensions validated point computation, making errors hard trace. Model metadata, cue labels, decision rules loosely coupled distributional parameters. Method dispatch split across ad-hoc S3 methods, legacy S4 classes, family-specific wrapper functions. S7 class architecture replaces strongly typed, validated, composable objects: Category Representations (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation): Distributional beliefs single category continuous multidimensional cue space (e.g., Gaussian [UVG/MVG/MUVG], Normal-Inverse-Wishart [NIW], Normal-Inverse-χ2\chi^2 [NIX/MNIX], exemplar sets). Category Representation Templates (MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate): Sets category representations sharing common cue space coordinate system. Cognitive Decision Models (MVBU_CognitiveModel): Complete observer adaptor models composing category template category priors P(c)P(c), decision rules (e.g., criterion, proportional, sampling), internal perceptual noise, lapse behaviors. Collections Cognitive Models (MVBU_ModelList): Strongly typed, ordered collections cognitive decision models across experimental conditions, exposure blocks, updating trajectories. Stan Input & Fit Objects (MVBU_Staninput, MVBU_Stanfit, MVBU_StanfitPosterior): Typed data bundles Bayesian posterior fits incremental belief-updating models. Underpinning classes Model Family System (MVBU_Family): registry pattern decouples mathematical functions governing category density evaluation, observation sampling, expected moment calculations object definitions.

code: # Multivariate Gaussian: mean vector mu and covariance matrix Sigma mu_b <- c(F1 = 350, F2 = 1100) Sigma_b <- matrix(c(2500, 500, 500, 3600),   nrow = 2, ncol = 2,   dimnames = list(names(mu_b), names(mu_b)) )  rep_b <- new_mvg_category_representation(   category_labels = "/b/",   cue_labels = c("F1", "F2"),   mu = mu_b,   Sigma = Sigma_b ) rep_b #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_CategoryRepresentation> #>   Category: /b/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   mu: c( 350, 1100) #>   Sigma: #>      F1   F2 #> F1 2500  500 #> F2  500 3600  # MUVG: Multivariate Univariate Gaussian (diagonal variances sigma2) rep_muvg_custom <- new_muvg_category_representation(   category_labels = "/b/",   cue_labels = c("F1", "F2"),   mu = mu_b,   sigma2 = c(F1 = 2500, F2 = 3600) ) rep_muvg_custom #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MUVG_CategoryRepresentation> #>   Category: /b/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   mu: c( 350, 1100) #>   sigma2: c(2500, 3600) rep_niw_custom <- new_niw_category_representation(   category_labels = "/b/",   cue_labels = c("F1", "F2"),   m = c(F1 = 350, F2 = 1100),   S = matrix(c(25000, 5000, 5000, 36000), nrow = 2, ncol = 2),   kappa = 10,   nu = 12 ) rep_niw_custom #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::NIW_CategoryRepresentation> #>   Category: /b/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   kappa: 10 #>   nu: 12 #>   m: c( 350, 1100) #>   S: #>       [,1]  [,2] #> [1,] 25000  5000 #> [2,]  5000 36000  # MNIX (Multivariate Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared for independent cues) rep_mnix_custom <- new_mnix_category_representation(   category_labels = "/b/",   cue_labels = c("F1", "F2"),   m = c(F1 = 350, F2 = 1100),   sigma2 = c(F1 = 2500, F2 = 3600),   kappa = c(F1 = 10, F2 = 10),   nu = c(F1 = 12, F2 = 12) ) rep_mnix_custom #> <MNIX_CategoryRepresentation> #>   Category: /b/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   kappa: c(10, 10) #>   nu: c(12, 12) #>   m: c( 350, 1100) #>   sigma2: c(2500, 3600)

text: cognitive model combines category template : category_prior: Prior probabilities P(c)P(c) across categories (must sum 1). decision_rule: posterior probabilities map categorization responses ("criterion", "proportional", "sampling"). lapse_rate lapse_bias: Probability distribution lapse responses (unrelated cue values). Sigma_noise noise_treatment: Internal perceptual noise covariance handling ("no_noise", "sample", "marginalize"). Similarly, empirical constructors can build complete cognitive model directly data single step:
code: # Instantiate an Ideal Observer model from the template observer_model <- new_mvg_ideal_observer(   category_template = tpl_empirical,   category_prior = c("/i/" = 0.5, "/u/" = 0.5),   decision_rule = "proportional",   lapse_rate = 0.02 ) observer_model #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_IdealObserver> #>   Categories (2): /i/, /u/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   Decision rule: proportional #>   Category prior: /i/: 0.5, /u/: 0.5 #>   Lapse rate: 0.02 (treatment: marginalize) #>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise) #>   Category representations (2): #>     /i/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /u/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) model_from_data <- new_mvg_ideal_observer_from_data(   data = train_data,   category = "category",   cues = c("F1", "F2"),   decision_rule = "criterion" ) model_from_data #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_IdealObserver> #>   Categories (2): /i/, /u/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   Decision rule: criterion #>   Category prior: /i/: 0.5, /u/: 0.5 #>   Lapse rate: 0 (treatment: no_lapses) #>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise) #>   Category representations (2): #>     /i/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /u/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2))

what: Multi-Cue Integration Models (Early vs. Late Integration)
title: S7 Class Architecture, Constructors, and Workflows
text: categorization involves multiple acoustic perceptual cues (e.g., F1F_1, F2F_2, duration, VOT), cognitive architectures differ fundamentally cue combination occurs relative category belief representation adaptation: MNIX_IdealAdaptor_IdealIntegrator: Unweighted Bayes rule integration across cues: log⁡p(𝐱∣c)=∑k=1Dlog⁡p(xk∣c)\log p(\mathbf{x} \mid c) = \sum_{k=1}^D \log p(x_k \mid c) MNIX_IdealAdaptor_WeightedIntegrator: Global attention/precision simplex weights 𝐰\mathbf{w} (wk≥0,∑kwk=1w_k \ge 0, \sum_k w_k = 1): log⁡p(𝐱∣c)=∑k=1Dwklog⁡p(xk∣c)\log p(\mathbf{x} \mid c) = \sum_{k=1}^D w_k \log p(x_k \mid c) MNIX_IdealAdaptor_CategoryWeightedIntegrator: Category-specific attention simplex weights 𝐰c\mathbf{w}_c: log⁡p(𝐱∣c)=∑k=1Dwc,klog⁡p(xk∣c)\log p(\mathbf{x} \mid c) = \sum_{k=1}^D w_{c, k} \log p(x_k \mid c) MNIX_IdealAdaptor: Dynamic cue weights driven empirical cue informativity marginal category overlap. IdealIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptor: Multi-cue input projected via fixed weights z=𝐰T𝐱z = \mathbf{w}^T \mathbf{x}, evaluated univariate 1D category representations. WeightedIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptor: Multi-cue input projected via subjective simplex weights 𝐰\mathbf{w} z=𝐰T𝐱z = \mathbf{w}^T \mathbf{x}. CategoryWeightedIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptor: Category-specific projection weights 𝐰c\mathbf{w}_c map cues category-specific 1D decision variables zc=𝐰cT𝐱z_c = \mathbf{w}_c^T \mathbf{x}.
code: # Example: Construct an early integrator MNIX model with 2 cues nix_tpl_1d <- example_category_representation_template("NIX") mod_early_weighted <- WeightedIntegrator_MNIX_IdealAdaptor(   category_template = nix_tpl_1d,   weights = c(F1 = 0.6, F2 = 0.4),   cues = c("F1", "F2") )  # Example: Construct a late integrator MNIX model with category-specific weights mnix_tpl_2d <- example_category_representation_template("MNIX") mod_late_cat <- MNIX_IdealAdaptor_CategoryWeightedIntegrator(   category_template = mnix_tpl_2d,   weights = rbind("/b/" = c(0.7, 0.3), "/d/" = c(0.4, 0.6)) )

text: MVBeliefUpdatr, model parameters standardized across four architectural tiers via metadata$parameters property get_parameters() generic: Category Representation (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation): Contains named list parameters defining specific category (e.g., mu Sigma Gaussian families, m, S, kappa, nu NIW/NIX). Category Representation Template (MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate): Contains named list aggregating category’s parameter list, indexed category label (lapply(template@representations, get_parameters)). Cognitive Model (MVBU_CognitiveModel): Contains parameter list underlying category template. Model List (MVBU_ModelList): Contains named list aggregating parameter lists constituent cognitive model, indexed model label (lapply(models, get_parameters)). Across four tiers, x@metadata$parameters guaranteed present, meaning downstream workflows can rely uniformly get_parameters(x):

text: Bayesian belief-updating models (NIW, NIX, MNIX), category representations encode joint distribution category mean 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu} covariance 𝚺\boldsymbol{\Sigma}. Downstream inferences distinguish two related distinct category moments: Expected Moments (get_expected_mu, get_expected_sigma): Conditional current hyperparameters, point expectation distribution parameters: 𝔼[𝛍]=𝐦,𝔼[𝚺]=𝐒ν−D−1\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol{\mu}] = \mathbf{m}, \qquad \mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}] = \frac{\mathbf{S}}{\nu - D - 1} represents expected category distribution current belief state. Marginal Moments (get_marginal_mu, get_marginal_sigma): Marginalizing parameter uncertainty category mean 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}: 𝛍marg=𝐦,𝚺marg=κ+1κ𝐒ν−D−1\boldsymbol{\mu}_{\text{marg}} = \mathbf{m}, \qquad \boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\text{marg}} = \frac{\kappa + 1}{\kappa} \frac{\mathbf{S}}{\nu - D - 1} observer finite confidence κ\kappa category mean 𝛍\boldsymbol{\mu}, marginal predictive distribution new observations xx increased dispersion scaled κ+1κ=1+1κ\frac{\kappa + 1}{\kappa} = 1 + \frac{1}{\kappa}. exposure sample size N→∞N \\infty (κ→∞\kappa \\infty), marginal covariance 𝚺marg\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{\text{marg}} converges expected covariance 𝔼[𝚺]\mathbb{E}[\boldsymbol{\Sigma}].

text: Category representations provide optional category_likelihood_function property defaults NULL. NULL, get_category_likelihood_function() automatically looks registered model family descriptor via get_family(rep) wraps density_function directly, incorporating decision noise log-transformation settings. Consequently, whenever model family registered registry, downstream operations (likelihood(), posterior(), categorize(), evaluate_model()) work immediately box. Evaluate category likelihoods p(x∣c)p(x \mid c) posterior probabilities P(c∣x)P(c \mid x) new observations:
code: # New test observations in cue space: # Point 1: clearly within /i/ # Point 2: near the category boundary (F1 = 464.5 Hz, F2 = 1598 Hz) # Point 3: clearly within /u/ test_points <- matrix(   c(     320, 2100,     444.5, 1598,     580, 1150   ),   nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE,   dimnames = list(c("clear_i", "boundary", "clear_u"), c("F1", "F2")) )  # Compute category likelihoods lik_mat <- likelihood(observer_model, test_points) lik_mat #>               /i/          /u/ #> [1,] 2.136194e-05 1.024496e-73 #> [2,] 1.241329e-24 1.047051e-22 #> [3,] 3.094133e-69 4.760218e-05  # Compute posterior category probabilities P(c | x) post_mat <- posterior(observer_model, test_points) post_mat #>             /i/       /u/ #> [1,] 0.99000000 0.0100000 #> [2,] 0.02148224 0.9785178 #> [3,] 0.01000000 0.9900000

text: function categorize() applies decision rule map observer’s posterior belief distribution P(c∣x)P(c \mid x) categorization responses. package supports three decision rules: decision_rule = "criterion" (Deterministic MAP / Optimal): Deterministically selects category maximizes posterior probability (maximum posteriori / argmax): ĉ=arg⁡maxcP(c∣x)\hat{c} = \arg\max_c P(c \mid x) optimal rule minimizes expected classification error 0-1 loss. decision_rule = "proportional" (Luce Choice / Probability Matching): Response choice probabilities match posterior probabilities: P(Response=c∣x)=P(c∣x)P(\text{Response} = c \mid x) = P(c \mid x) computing categorization probabilities evaluating model likelihoods evaluate_model(), "proportional" represents smooth probability matching across stimulus space. decision_rule = "sampling" (Posterior Sampling): Generates discrete category choice sampled stochastically categorical distribution defined P(c∣x)P(c \mid x): ĉ∼Categorical(P(c1∣x),…,P(cK∣x))\hat{c} \sim \text{Categorical}(P(c_1 \mid x), \dots, P(c_K \mid x)) Across repeated trials, empirical frequency choices converges proportional posterior probabilities. Let’s evaluate test observations decision rule:
code: # 1. Deterministic MAP classification ("criterion") # At the boundary point, the category with max posterior probability is # chosen deterministically cat_criterion <- categorize(   observer_model,   test_points,   decision_rule = "criterion" ) cat_criterion #> [1] "/i/" "/u/" "/u/"  # 2. Probability matching ("proportional") # Reports the model's posterior probability matching classification cat_proportional <- categorize(   observer_model,   test_points,   decision_rule = "proportional" ) cat_proportional #>   response_category response_probability #> 1               /i/            0.9900000 #> 2               /u/            0.9785178 #> 3               /u/            0.9900000  # 3. Stochastic posterior sampling ("sampling") # Produces stochastic discrete choices weighted by P(c | x) set.seed(42) cat_sampling_1 <- categorize(   observer_model,   test_points,   decision_rule = "sampling" ) cat_sampling_1 #> [1] "/i/" "/u/" "/u/"  # A second independent sampling run reflects trial-by-trial stochasticity # at the boundary set.seed(101) cat_sampling_2 <- categorize(   observer_model,   test_points,   decision_rule = "sampling" ) cat_sampling_2 #> [1] "/i/" "/u/" "/u/"

title: S7 Class Architecture, Constructors, and Workflows
text: Consider three individual observer models representing vowel categories distinctly different estimated means covariances (e.g., positive correlation, negative correlation, uncorrelated cues): see category representation parameters change aggregation, can explicitly compare category means (μ\mu) covariance matrices (Σ\Sigma) aggregation: can also visualize category likelihood ellipses individual models MVBU_ModelList alongside aggregated model:
code:
library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)  # Individual Observer 1: Positive cue covariance, shifted top-left mvg1 <- new_mvg_ideal_observer(   category_template = new_category_representation_template(     representations = list(       "/i/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/i/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(250, 2400), Sigma = matrix(c(800, 600, 600, 3000), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2")))),       "/u/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/u/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(420, 1200), Sigma = matrix(c(900, 500, 500, 2500), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2"))))     )   ),   lapse_rate = 0.01 )  # Individual Observer 2: Negative cue covariance and larger variance, shifted right mvg2 <- new_mvg_ideal_observer(   category_template = new_category_representation_template(     representations = list(       "/i/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/i/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(350, 2200), Sigma = matrix(c(2000, -1200, -1200, 6000), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2")))),       "/u/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/u/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(580, 1000), Sigma = matrix(c(1800, -800, -800, 4500), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2"))))     )   ),   lapse_rate = 0.05 )  # Individual Observer 3: Uncorrelated cues, shifted down mvg3 <- new_mvg_ideal_observer(   category_template = new_category_representation_template(     representations = list(       "/i/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/i/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(300, 2000), Sigma = matrix(c(1200, 0, 0, 4000), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2")))),       "/u/" = new_mvg_category_representation("/u/", c("F1", "F2"), mu = c(500, 800), Sigma = matrix(c(1500, 0, 0, 3500), 2, 2, dimnames = list(c("F1", "F2"), c("F1", "F2"))))     )   ),   lapse_rate = 0.03 )  # Bundle individual models into an MVBU_ModelList container mvg_list <- as_model_list(   list(Model_1 = mvg1, Model_2 = mvg2, Model_3 = mvg3) )  # Inspect individual models before aggregation cat("--- Model List ---
") #> --- Model List --- print(mvg_list) #> <MVBU_ModelList>  # Aggregate all three models via MVBU_ModelList (unweighted mean) mvg_aggregated <- aggregate_models(mvg_list)  cat("
--- Aggregated MVG Model ---
") #>  #> --- Aggregated MVG Model --- mvg_aggregated #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_IdealObserver> #>   Categories (2): /i/, /u/ #>   Cues (2): F1, F2 #>   Decision rule: sampling #>   Category prior: /i/: 0.5, /u/: 0.5 #>   Lapse rate: 0.03 (treatment: marginalize) #>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise) #>   Category representations (2): #>     /i/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /u/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) # Compare category parameters before and after aggregation for (cat_name in c("/i/", "/u/")) {   cat(sprintf("
=== Category: %s ===
", cat_name))   cat("Model 1 mu:", mvg1@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@mu, "
")   cat("Model 2 mu:", mvg2@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@mu, "
")   cat("Model 3 mu:", mvg3@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@mu, "
")   cat("Aggregated mu:", mvg_aggregated@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@mu, "

")    cat("Model 1 Sigma:
")   print(mvg1@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@Sigma)   cat("Model 2 Sigma:
")   print(mvg2@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@Sigma)   cat("Model 3 Sigma:
")   print(mvg3@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@Sigma)   cat("Aggregated Sigma:
")   print(mvg_aggregated@category_template@representations[[cat_name]]@Sigma) } #>  #> === Category: /i/ === #> Model 1 mu: 250 2400  #> Model 2 mu: 350 2200  #> Model 3 mu: 300 2000  #> Aggregated mu: 300 2200  #>  #> Model 1 Sigma: #>     F1   F2 #> F1 800  600 #> F2 600 3000 #> Model 2 Sigma: #>       F1    F2 #> F1  2000 -1200 #> F2 -1200  6000 #> Model 3 Sigma: #>      F1   F2 #> F1 1200    0 #> F2    0 4000 #> Aggregated Sigma: #>          F1       F2 #> F1 1333.333 -200.000 #> F2 -200.000 4333.333 #>  #> === Category: /u/ === #> Model 1 mu: 420 1200  #> Model 2 mu: 580 1000  #> Model 3 mu: 500 800  #> Aggregated mu: 500 1000  #>  #> Model 1 Sigma: #>     F1   F2 #> F1 900  500 #> F2 500 2500 #> Model 2 Sigma: #>      F1   F2 #> F1 1800 -800 #> F2 -800 4500 #> Model 3 Sigma: #>      F1   F2 #> F1 1500    0 #> F2    0 3500 #> Aggregated Sigma: #>      F1   F2 #> F1 1400 -100 #> F2 -100 3500 # Faceted plot of all individual models in the ModelList p_individuals <- plot_categories(mvg_list, mode = "facet", interactive = FALSE) p_agg <- plot(mvg_aggregated) + ggtitle("Aggregated Model (Average)")  p_individuals / (plot_spacer() + p_agg + plot_spacer())

title: Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, and Belief Updating
text: Visualizing distributional representations response probabilities essential understanding multidimensional category structures, decision boundaries, belief updating. MVBeliefUpdatr package provides unified, highly extensible visualization system built top ggplot2 plotly. returned ggplot plotly objects can customized native ggplot2 plotly layers, color scales, facets, themes. Every visualization function package dispatches new S7 class architecture, accepting: Single category representations (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation) Multi-category templates (MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate) Complete cognitive decision models (MVBU_CognitiveModel) Fitted Bayesian models (MVBU_Stanfit) Interactive Rendered Visualizations: view vignette rendered figures, interactive 3D WebGL scenes, animated belief updates, visit online documentation : https://hlplab.github.io/MVBeliefUpdatr/articles/visualizing-models--categories.html. local interactive R sessions, code examples can executed directly RStudio inspect customize figures.
code: library(MVBeliefUpdatr) library(ggplot2) library(patchwork)

title: Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, and Belief Updating
text: plot_categories() generic visualizes distributional layout category beliefs cue space. Users can select cues plot cues argument: cues: Character vector cues plotted. default, many cues contained category representation(s), maximum three cues. three cues, first three cues plotted. Selecting fewer full set cues causes function marginalize unplotted cues. categories: Optional character vector subset category labels plot (e.g., categories = c("/b/", "/d/")). Defaults categories.

title: Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, and Belief Updating
text: one cue selected plotting (length(cues) == 1L), category representations visualized univariate probability density functions p(x∣c)p(x \mid c). Core arguments (listed order function signature): aes: Aesthetic layer type ("contour" density line curves, "fill-discrete" alias "fill" shaded density ribbons; "fill-gradient" yields equivalent continuous density shading). limits: 2-element numeric vector c(min, max) named list list(cue = c(min, max)) specifying axis bounds. Defaults span plotted distributions across categories. resolution: Number evaluation points along continuous cue grid (default 200). arguments ignored.  applied multi-category template cognitive model, categories plotted simultaneously unified color mapping shared legend:
code: # Construct a 1D MVG category representation for /b/ along Voice-Onset Time (ms) rep_1d_mvg <- example_mvg_category_representation(n_cues = 1, category = "/b/") p_1d_rep <- plot_categories(rep_1d_mvg) p_1d_rep # 1D MVG multi-category template (/b/, /d/, /g/) tpl_1d_mvg <- example_mvg_category_representation_template(n_cues = 1, categories = c("/b/", "/d/", "/g/"))  # Left: Line contour curves (default aes = 'contour') p_tpl_line <- plot_categories(tpl_1d_mvg, limits = c(-50, 120)) +   labs(title = "Line Density (default aes = 'contour')")  # Right: Shaded density ribbons (aes = 'fill') p_tpl_fill <- plot_categories(tpl_1d_mvg, aes = "fill", limits = c(-50, 120)) +   labs(title = "Shaded Ribbon (aes = 'fill')")  p_tpl_line + p_tpl_fill + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

title: Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, and Belief Updating
text: two cues selected plotting (length(cues) == 2L), category representations can visualized using covariance ellipses, continuous density gradients, discrete density bands. Core arguments (order function signature): "contour": Draws boundary contour lines (covariance ellipses parametric models; 2D KDE contours exemplar models). "fill-discrete" (alias "fill"): Shaded discrete confidence regions colored category. "fill-gradient": Continuous density heatmap alpha proportional p(𝐱∣c)p(\mathbf{x} \mid c). Combinations like c("fill-gradient", "contour") c("fill-discrete", "contour"). fill contour aesthetics present, fill color keys automatically unified single legend. levels: Central probability mass regions enclose (defaulting levels = 2 * pnorm(1:3) - 1 ≈0.683,0.954,0.997\approx 0.683, 0.954, 0.997). Users can specify custom regions, levels = c(0.50, 0.95) 50% 95% intervals. limits: Coordinate bounds along axes. Specified named list (e.g., limits = list(VOT = c(-30, 90), f0_semitones = c(-4, 6))) 2-element numeric vector c(min, max) applied dimensions. "fill-gradient" used, density raster tiles seamlessly cover entire plotted space panel boundaries without artificial padding. resolution: Grid density along cue axis (default 100).
code: tpl_2d_mvg <- example_mvg_category_representation_template(n_cues = 2)  # Mode 1: Custom 50% and 95% central probability contours for /b/ and /p/ p_2d_contour <- plot_categories(   tpl_2d_mvg,   categories = c("/b/", "/p/"),   aes = "contour",   levels = c(0.50, 0.95),   limits = list(VOT = c(-30, 90), f0_semitones = c(-4, 6)) ) + labs(title = "50% & 95% Central Contours")  # Mode 2: Continuous density gradient + contour borders for /b/ and /p/ p_2d_combined <- plot_categories(   tpl_2d_mvg,   categories = c("/b/", "/p/"),   aes = c("fill-gradient", "contour"),   limits = list(VOT = c(-30, 90), f0_semitones = c(-4, 6)) ) + labs(title = "Gradient Fill + Contours")  p_2d_contour + p_2d_combined + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

P(c∣𝐱)P(c \mid \mathbf{x}) posterior response probability derived generative model: P(c∣𝐱)=p(𝐱∣c)P(c)∑kp(𝐱∣k)P(k)P(c \mid \mathbf{x}) = \frac{p(\mathbf{x} \mid c) P(c)}{\sum_{k} p(\mathbf{x} \mid k) P(k)} according chosen decision_rule (e.g., "proportional" probability matching "criterion" deterministic winner-take-classification). introduction lapse rates, category biases, perceptual noise speech categorization models, see Xie, Jaeger, & Kurumada (2023). Core Arguments plot_categorization_functions include: cues: Character vector cue dimensions plot (1, 2, 3 cues; defaults many cues possible 3, selecting first cues model). categories: Optional character vector specifying subset category labels evaluate plot (defaults first category). "proportional": Response probability equals posterior probability P(c∣𝐱)P(c \mid \mathbf{x}) (probability matching). "criterion": Deterministic maximum posteriori rule (winner-take-classification boundary). "sampling": Stochastic sampling category choices posterior beliefs. aes: Aesthetic layer type ("contour" decision boundary contours, "fill" "fill-gradient" continuous response probability heatmaps, "fill-discrete" winner-take-partition regions). Defaults "contour". limits: Axis bounds, specified 2-element vector c(min, max) named list list(VOT = c(-30, 90), f0_semitones = c(-4, 6)). resolution: Grid density along cue dimension (default 100). what: Posterior Category Beliefs: Marginalized vs. Sample Uncertainty
title: Visualizing Categories, Categorization Functions, and Belief Updating
text: Using plot_categories() MVBU_Stanfit object provides two complementary modes inspect posterior beliefs via uncertainty_treatment: uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize" (default): Marginalizes across selected posterior draws, plotting category distributions computed posterior parameter expectations marginal covariances. uncertainty_treatment = "sample": Evaluates category distributions across selected individual posterior MCMC draws, overlaying sample contours curves faithfully convey parameter estimation uncertainty. ndraws: Integer specifying number posterior draws sample display (default 20).
code: # Load or fit 2D NIW ideal adaptor model models_dir <- if (dir.exists("../tests/testthat/models")) {   "../tests/testthat/models" } else if (dir.exists("tests/testthat/models")) {   "tests/testthat/models" } else {   tempdir() } fit_path <- file.path(   models_dir,   "minimal-niw_ideal_adaptor-NIW-2cue.rds" ) fit <- example_ideal_adaptor_stanfit(   model_family = "NIW",   n_cues = 2L,   file = fit_path,   file_refit = "never" )  # 1. Marginalized Posterior Representation (uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize") p_fit_marg <- plot_categories(fit, uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize") +   labs(title = "Marginalized (uncertainty_treatment = 'marginalize')")  # 2. Posterior Uncertainty Draws (uncertainty_treatment = "sample", ndraws = 20) p_fit_sample <- plot_categories(fit, uncertainty_treatment = "sample", ndraws = 20) +   labs(title = "Sample Draws (uncertainty_treatment = 'sample', ndraws = 20)")  p_fit_marg + p_fit_sample + plot_layout(guides = "collect")

Plot exposure and test observations from a Stan input object set.seed(42) sample_input <- new_ideal_adaptor_stanfit_input(   exposure = data.frame(     category = factor(rep(c("/b/", "/p/"), each = 30)),     group = factor(rep("Group1", 60)),     VOT = c(rnorm(30, 10, 8), rnorm(30, 45, 8)),     f0_semitones = c(rnorm(30, 2, 1), rnorm(30, 4, 1))   ),   test = data.frame(     response = factor(sample(c("/b/", "/p/"), 40, replace = TRUE)),     group = factor(rep("Group1", 40)),     VOT = runif(40, 0, 60),     f0_semitones = runif(40, 1, 5)   ),   cues = c("VOT", "f0_semitones"),   category = "category",   response = "response",   group = "group",   stanmodel = "NIW_ideal_adaptor" )  p_sample_all <- plot_sample(   sample_input,   aes = list(exposure = c("fill-gradient", "contour"), test = "points") ) + labs(title = "Exposure & Test Sample (Stan Input)")  # 2. text: reconstruct_update_history() generic reconstructs sequential belief updating directly fitted Bayesian model (MVBU_Stanfit), generating MVBU_ModelList checkpoint models along exposure sequence:  full posterior parameter uncertainty needs tracked across update checkpoint, uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize" updates posterior MCMC draw incrementally, returning MVBU_ModelList MVBU_StanfitPosterior objects:  Note interactive slider controls: explore belief updating decision surfaces interactively time slider rather multi-panel facets, specify mode = "animate", interactive = TRUE (e.g., plot_categories(hist_fast, mode = "animate", interactive = TRUE)). Multi-panel faceting (mode = "facet") produces tiled subplots across steps via ggplot2 (interactive = FALSE).
code: # 1. Fast mode: sequentially updates an ideal adaptor from prior marginal moments # Returns an MVBU_ModelList of MVBU_CognitiveModel objects hist_fast <- reconstruct_update_history(   fit,   uncertainty_treatment = "discard",   step_size = 40L )  # Plot category belief shifts across exposure steps (multi-panel facet grid) plot_categories(hist_fast, mode = "facet", interactive = FALSE) # 2. Full posterior mode: incrementally updates posterior draws (ndraws = 200) hist_full <- reconstruct_update_history(   fit,   uncertainty_treatment = "marginalize",   ndraws = 200L,   step_size = 40L )  # Faceted visualization of categorization decision functions across checkpoints plot_categorization_functions(hist_full, mode = "facet", interactive = FALSE)

title: MVBU Core S7 Class Architecture — MVBU-core-classes
text: metadata Optional list metadata. Defaults list(). category_template MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing category representations. decision_rule Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", "proportional". Defaults "sampling". category_prior Optional numeric vector prior category probabilities summing 1. Defaults equal priors. lapse_rate Numeric scalar lapse probability [0, 1]. Defaults 0. lapse_bias Optional numeric vector lapse category probabilities summing 1. Defaults uniform bias across categories. Sigma_noise Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix scalar variance. Defaults NULL. noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise evaluation updating: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". "no_noise": perceptual noise applied input cues, noise assumed categorization. "sample": Simulates sensory noise specific observation. Noise drawn \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) added input cues (projected composite cue space early integration), observer accounts noise uncertainty categorization adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) likelihood scale. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). noise sampled onto input stimulus, \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) added category covariance scale. Defaults .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" noise present, "no_noise" otherwise. lapse_treatment Treatment attentional lapses evaluation updating: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; categorization updating reflect pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs: categorization, posterior replaced lapse_bias; updating, lapsing observation treated uninformative. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). category posterior mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\), evidence updating downweighted \(1 - \lambda\). Defaults .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise.

title: MVBU Core S7 Class Architecture — MVBU-core-classes
text: MVBU_CategoryRepresentation defines structure one category-level representational object. uni- multivariate Gaussian, mixture Gaussians, exemplar-based representation. MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate collects one category-representation objects validated set used model. corresponds notion "templates" e.g., (Nearey Assmann 2007) . MVBU_CognitiveModel combines category-template structure model-level decision behavior (decision_rule, category_prior, lapse_rate, lapse_bias). Family-level semantics layered top base classes. Ideal observer/adaptor pairings follow: UVG_IdealObserver UVG <-> NIX_IdealAdaptor NIX MUVG_IdealObserver MUVG <-> MNIX_IdealAdaptor MNIX MVG_IdealObserver MVG <-> NIW_IdealAdaptor NIW Exemplar_Model EXEMPLAR treated standalone family.

fixing category representation parameters, note distinction prior hyperparameters, expected prior moments, known category parameters: "m_0" "S_0" Prior hyperparameters conjugate prior distribution (Normal-Inverse-Wishart Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared). Fixing either moments determines conjugate belief updating predictive likelihood behavior: Case 1 (unknown) Standard NIW NIX conjugate updating mean covariance; predictive likelihood Student-\(t\). u_n = 
u_0 + n\), \(S_n = S_0 +         \sum (x_i - \mu_0)(x_i - \mu_0)^T\)). mean known, predictive likelihood Student-\(t\) \(
u_n\) degrees freedom scale \(S_n / (
u_n - K + 1)\) (\(S_n /

what: MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors — MVBeliefUpdatr-package
title: MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors — MVBeliefUpdatr-package
text: Model, fit, visualize incremental Bayesian categorization belief updating uni- multivariate Gaussian, cue integration, exemplar-based cognitive models using 'S7' class architecture. Provides tools simulating normative ideal observers ideal adaptors conjugate priors including Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (NIX), Multivariate Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (MNIX), Normal-Inverse-Wishart (NIW) distributions. Supports Bayesian parameter inference via Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) sampling using 'Stan', model comparison via 'loo', rich visualizations 'ggplot2' 'patchwork'.

title: MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors — MVBeliefUpdatr-package
text: MVBeliefUpdatr provides unified, object-oriented framework Bayesian ideal observers, ideal adaptors, incremental belief updating, hierarchical Bayesian cognitive modeling. package supports continuous distributional representations (univariate Gaussian, multivariate Gaussian, multi-univariate Gaussian cue integration), conjugate prior distributions category parameters (Normal-Inverse- Chisquare, Normal-Inverse-Wishart), exemplar-based representations. Using analytical conjugate updating hierarchical Bayesian inference Stan via rstan, MVBeliefUpdatr facilitates simulation, parameter estimation, categorization prediction, visualization speech perception perceptual adaptation experiments.

title: MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors — MVBeliefUpdatr-package
text: model objects organized explicit, compositional S7 class hierarchy: MVBU_CategoryRepresentation Abstract base class individual category representations, encapsulating category parameters, cue labels, likelihood functions. MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate Validated collection category representations forming perceptual inventory template. MVBU_CognitiveModel Decision model pairing category template decision behavior (decision rule, category priors, lapse rate, lapse bias, perceptual noise). MVBU_IdealObserver Subclass MVBU_CognitiveModel observers fixed generative category distributions. MVBU_IdealAdaptor Subclass MVBU_CognitiveModel adaptors conjugate prior beliefs update incrementally exposure. MVBU_Stanfit Wrapper rstan stanfit objects inferring prior beliefs, lapse parameters, noise behavioral test data. MVBU_StanfitInput Container exposure data, test data, priors, transformation functions used prepare Stan inputs. MVBU_Staninput Validated input data list passed Stan models.

title: MVBeliefUpdatr: Fitting, Summarizing, and Visualizing of Gaussian Ideal Observers and Adaptors — MVBeliefUpdatr-package
text: MVBeliefUpdatr provides concrete S7 classes constructors across seven families: UVG / NIX Univariate Gaussian ideal observers (UVG_IdealObserver) Normal-Inverse-Chisquare ideal adaptors (NIX_IdealAdaptor). MUVG / MNIX Multi-univariate Gaussian ideal observers (MUVG_IdealObserver) independent Normal-Inverse-Chisquare cue integration adaptors (MNIX_IdealAdaptor). MVG / NIW Multivariate Gaussian ideal observers (MVG_IdealObserver) Normal-Inverse-Wishart ideal adaptors (NIW_IdealAdaptor). EXEMPLAR Exemplar-based categorization models (Exemplar_Model) kernel density estimation stored exemplars.

u - D - 1)\). marginal_moments Distribution summary table across posterior draws category mean \(\mu\) marginal predictive covariance \(\Sigma_{	ext{marg}} =  rac{\kappa + 1}         {\kappa} \Sigma_{	ext{exp}}\). likelihood_function Closure evaluating category likelihoods aggregated point estimates. posterior_function Closure evaluating category posterior probabilities aggregated point estimates.

text: Supported evaluation methods include: "log_lik": Trial--trial categorical log-likelihood (default): $$\log L_{\text{cat}} = \sum_{=1}^N \log P(Y = y_i \mid X = x_i) = \sum_{u=1}^U \sum_{j=1}^K n_{u,j} \log p_{u,j}$$ \(u\) indexes unique stimulus locations, \(j\) indexes categories, \(n_{u,j}\) count responses category \(j\) stimulus \(u\), \(p_{u,j}\) model's predicted probability category \(j\) \(u\). represents log probability observing exact sequence individual responses \((y_1, \dots, y_N)\). standard likelihood metric GLMs, logistic regression, Bayesian Stan models. "accuracy": Proportion correct / matching responses. "likelihood---constant": Deprecated alias "log_lik" (supported version 0.1). Additionally, following method available support calculation order invariant log-likelihoods: "log_lik_permutation_constant": log multinomial combinatorial permutation factor: $$C = \sum_{u=1}^U \left( \log(N_u!) - \sum_{j=1}^K \log(n_{u,j}!) \right) = \sum_{u=1}^U \log \binom{N_u}{n_{u,1}, \dots, n_{u,K}}$$ \(N_u = \sum_j n_{u,j}\) total number presentations stimulus location \(u\). factor accounts permutations response order stimulus location. Crucially, \(C\) depends purely observed data completely independent cognitive model.

title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: metadata Optional list metadata. exemplars Numeric matrix data frame exemplars (rows exemplars; columns correspond cue_labels). exemplar_weights Optional numeric vector exemplar weights [0, 1] summing 1. Defaults equal weights (1 / n_exemplars). c Optional positive numeric scalar specifying sensitivity / inverse kernel bandwidth scale. NULL (default), c estimated adaptively via Silverman's (1986) multivariate rule thumb: $$h^2 = \left(\frac{4}{(d + 2) n}\right)^{\frac{2}{d + 4}}, \quad c = \frac{1}{2 h^2}$$ category_labels Character vector category label(s). cue_labels Character vector cue dimension label(s). data Data frame containing category cue observations. category Character string indicating category column data. Defaults "category". cues Character vector indicating cue columns data. category_template MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing Exemplar category representations. decision_rule Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", "proportional". Defaults "sampling". category_prior Optional numeric vector prior category probabilities summing 1. Defaults equal priors. lapse_rate Numeric scalar lapse probability [0, 1]. Defaults 0. lapse_bias Optional numeric vector lapse category probabilities summing 1. Sigma_noise Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix. noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise evaluation: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". "no_noise": perceptual noise applied input cues, noise assumed categorization. "sample": Simulates sensory noise specific observation. Noise drawn \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) added input cues, observer accounts noise uncertainty categorization adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) likelihood scale. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). noise sampled onto input stimulus, \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) added category covariance scale. Defaults .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" noise present, "no_noise" otherwise. lapse_treatment Treatment attentional lapses evaluation: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; categorization reflects pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs: posterior replaced lapse_bias. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). category posterior mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\). Defaults .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise.

what: Relation to the Generalized Context Model (GCM)
title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: Generalized Context Model (Nosofsky 1986; Kruschke 1992) , psychological similarity observed stimulus \(\mathbf{x}\) stored exemplar \(\mathbf{e}_i\) given : $$\operatorname{sim}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_i) = \exp\left(-c \cdot d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_i)^p\right)$$ \(c > 0\) perceptual sensitivity parameter \(d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_i)\) attention-weighted Minkowski distance: $$d(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_i) = \left(\sum_{k=1}^d w_k |x_k - e_{,k}|^\tau\right)^{\frac{1}{\tau}}$$ attention weights \(w_k\) (\(\sum w_k = 1\)). Luce choice rule category response biases \(b_C\), categorization probability GCM : $$P(C \mid \mathbf{x}) = \frac{b_C \sum_{j \C} \operatorname{sim}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_{C,j})}{ \sum_K b_K \sum_{j \K} \operatorname{sim}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_{K,j})}$$

title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: MVBeliefUpdatr, category representations framed terms probability density estimation (Ashby Alfonso-Reese 1995; Shi et al. 2010) : $$p(\mathbf{x} \mid C) = \sum_{=1}^n \pi_{C,} \, \mathcal{N}\left(\mathbf{x} \mid \mathbf{e}_{C,}, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{kernel}}\right)$$ kernel covariance matched GCM sensitivity attention: $$\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{kernel}}^{-1} = 2c \mathbf{W} \iff \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{kernel}} = \frac{1}{2c} \mathbf{W}^{-1}$$ Gaussian likelihood directly proportional GCM similarity: $$\mathcal{N}\left(\mathbf{x} \mid \mathbf{e}_i, \mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{kernel}}\right) \propto \operatorname{sim}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{e}_i)$$ plugged Bayes' rule \(P(C \mid \mathbf{x}) = \frac{P(C) p(\mathbf{x} \mid C)}{\sum_K P(K) p(\mathbf{x} \mid K)}\), normalizing constant cancels , resulting exact mathematical equivalence GCM (Ashby Alfonso-Reese 1995) .

title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: density-based formulation corresponds GCM two specific geometric assumptions: Euclidean distance metric (\(\tau = 2\)): Assumes integral (holistic) perceptual dimensions dimensions combine Euclidean-wise (Shepard 1987; Nosofsky 1986) . Gaussian similarity gradient (\(p = 2\)): Assumes Gaussian similarity decay profile \(\exp(-c \cdot d^2)\) rather exponential profile \(\exp(-c \cdot d)\), characteristic integral dimensions Gaussian kernel density estimators. addition, MVBeliefUpdatr generalizes standard GCM allowing full covariance matrix \(\mathbf{\Sigma}_{\text{kernel}} = \frac{1}{2c}\operatorname{Cov}(\mathbf{X})\), accommodating correlated cue dimensions (e.g., acoustic formant cues).

title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: c provided (NULL), c defaults Silverman's (1986) multivariate rule--thumb bandwidth factor: $$h^2 = \left(\frac{4}{(d + 2) n}\right)^{\frac{2}{d + 4}}, \quad c = \frac{1}{2 h^2}$$ asymptotically minimizes Mean Integrated Squared Error (MISE) true category distribution.

title: Exemplar Model Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-exemplar
text: Nosofsky RM (1986). “Attention, similarity, identification–categorization relationship.” Journal Experimental Psychology: General, 115(1), 39. Shepard RN (1987). “Toward universal law generalization psychological science.” Science, 237(4820), 1317–1323. Ashby FG, Alfonso-Reese PC (1995). “Categorization probability density estimation.” Journal Mathematical Psychology, 39(2), 216–233. Kruschke JK (1992). “ALCOVE: exemplar-based connectionist model category learning.” Psychological Review, 99(1), 22–44.

text: metadata Optional list metadata. Defaults list(). m Numeric vector per-cue location hyperparameters. kappa Positive numeric scalar vector precision scalings (\(\kappa > 0\)). late integration, vector length equal cues (scalar recycled across cues). early integration, scalar reflecting composite dimension belief strength. nu Positive numeric scalar vector degrees freedom (\(\nu > 2\)). late integration, vector length equal cues (scalar recycled across cues). early integration, scalar reflecting composite dimension degrees freedom. sigma2 Numeric vector per-cue scale parameters. weights Numeric vector matrix integration/attention weights. representations global weighted models, numeric simplex vector summing 1. category-weighted models, \(M \times K\) matrix whose rows sum 1. category_labels Character vector category label(s). cue_labels Character vector cue labels (least 2 cue dimensions). data Data frame containing category cue observations. category Character string indicating category column data. Defaults "category". cues Character vector indicating cue columns data (least 2 cues). ... Additional arguments passed methods constructors. category_template MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing MNIX category representations. decision_rule Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", "proportional". Defaults "sampling". category_prior Optional numeric vector prior category probabilities summing 1. Defaults equal priors. lapse_rate Numeric scalar lapse probability [0, 1]. Defaults 0. lapse_bias Optional numeric vector lapse category probabilities summing 1. Defaults uniform bias 1/M. Sigma_noise Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix vector. noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise evaluation updating: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". "no_noise": perceptual noise applied input cues, noise assumed categorization. "sample": Simulates sensory noise specific observation. Noise drawn \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) added input cues (projected composite cue space early integration), observer accounts noise uncertainty categorization adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) likelihood scale. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). noise sampled onto input stimulus, \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) added category covariance scale. Defaults .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" noise present, "no_noise" otherwise. lapse_treatment Treatment attentional lapses evaluation updating: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; categorization updating reflect pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs: categorization, posterior replaced lapse_bias; updating, lapsing observation treated uninformative. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). category posterior mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\), evidence updating downweighted \(1 - \lambda\). Defaults .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise. weights_matrix Deprecated. Use weights instead. input_cues Deprecated. Use cues instead.

title: Multi-Cue Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared (MNIX) Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-mnix
text: MNIX family unifies multi-cue belief updating late early integration regimes: Late Integration: Categories represented independent marginal Student-\(t\) predictive components along cue dimension (\(\kappa\) \(\nu\) length \(K\)). Cue log-likelihoods combined decision time via Bayes rule attention weights. Early Integration: Multi-cue observations projected composite dimension \(z = \mathbf{w}^\top \mathbf{x}\) prior updating (\(\kappa\) \(\nu\) scalar length 1).

title: Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared (NIX) Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-nix
text: metadata Optional list metadata. Defaults list(). m Numeric scalar location hyperparameter. kappa Positive numeric scalar precision scaling (\(\kappa > 0\)). nu Positive numeric scalar degrees freedom (\(\nu > 0\)). sigma2 Positive numeric scalar scale parameter (\(\sigma^2 > 0\)). category_labels Character vector category label(s). cue_labels Character vector cue label(s). NIX, exactly one cue dimension allowed. data Data frame containing category cue observations. category Character string indicating category column data. Defaults "category". cues Character string indicating cue column data. Defaults "cue". ... Additional arguments passed methods constructors. category_template MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate object containing NIX category representations. decision_rule Categorization decision rule: "sampling", "criterion", "proportional". Defaults "sampling". category_prior Optional numeric vector prior category probabilities summing 1. Defaults equal priors. lapse_rate Numeric scalar lapse probability [0, 1]. Defaults 0. lapse_bias Optional numeric vector lapse category probabilities summing 1. Defaults uniform bias 1/M. Sigma_noise Optional perceptual/measurement noise covariance matrix scalar variance. noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise evaluation updating: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". "no_noise": perceptual noise applied input cues, noise assumed categorization. "sample": Simulates sensory noise specific observation. Noise drawn \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) added input cues, observer accounts noise uncertainty categorization adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) likelihood scale. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). noise sampled onto input stimulus, \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) added category covariance scale. Defaults .infer_noise_treatment(Sigma_noise): "marginalize" noise present, "no_noise" otherwise. lapse_treatment Treatment attentional lapses evaluation updating: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; categorization updating reflect pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs: categorization, posterior replaced lapse_bias; updating, lapsing observation treated uninformative. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities). category posterior mixture \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\), evidence updating downweighted \(1 - \lambda\). Defaults .infer_lapse_treatment(lapse_rate): "marginalize" lapse_rate > 0, "no_lapses" otherwise.

title: Normal-Inverse-Chi-Squared (NIX) Family: Representations, Templates, and Models — family-nix
text: Normal-Inverse-\(\chi^2\) (NIX) family models adaptor-style uncertainty univariate Gaussian category structure. predictive likelihood Student-\(t\) distribution: \(s_c = \sqrt{\sigma_c^2(\kappa_c+1)/\kappa_c}\), $$p(x \mid c) =   \frac{1}{s_c} \, t_{\nu_c}\!\left(\frac{x-m_c}{s_c}\right)$$

title: Fit ideal adaptor — fit_ideal_adaptor
text: NIW_ideal_adaptor Normal-Inverse-Wishart (NIW) prior ideal adaptor. default model multivariate Gaussian categories. Accepts univariate multivariate input, though NIX model faster univariate input. NIX_ideal_adaptor Normal-Inverse-Chisquare (NIX) prior ideal adaptor univariate Gaussian categories. Accepts univariate input. MNIX_ideal_adaptor Separate NIXs multiple cues integrated categorization assuming ideal cue weights based relative informativity cue. interpreting inferred parameters, kept mind inferred scatter matrix (e.g., S_0 NIW model) includes variability internal perceptual /external environmental noise, addition motor noise reflected production data. also implies , Sigma_0 provided user arguably convolved estimate perceptual noise. particularly important data fitting contains test phases without exposure (e.g., pre-exposure tests). Use methods(class = "ideal_adaptor_stanfit") overview available methods.

title: Convert Between NIW/NIX Hyperparameters and Expected/Marginal Moments — get_expected_Sigma_from_S
text: S Scatter matrix \(S\) (numeric matrix, scalar, list matrices). nu Strength belief (pseudocount) \(\Sigma\) (\(\nu > D + 1\)). Sigma Expected category covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) (numeric matrix, scalar, list matrices). kappa Strength belief (pseudocount) \(\mu\). m Location hyperparameter \(m\) (numeric vector, matrix, list). mu Expected category mean vector \(\mu\) (numeric vector, matrix, list).

title: Convert Between NIW/NIX Hyperparameters and Expected/Marginal Moments — get_expected_Sigma_from_S
text:
get_expected_Sigma_from_S, expected covariance matrix \(\Sigma = S / (
u - D - 1)\). get_S_from_expected_Sigma, scatter matrix \(S = \Sigma \cdot (
u - D - 1)\). get_marginal_Sigma_from_S, marginal category covariance matrix \(\Sigma = (\kappa + 1) / \kappa \cdot S / (
u - D - 1)\). get_expected_mu_from_m get_m_from_expected_mu, mean vector location hyperparameter.

title: Convert Between NIW/NIX Hyperparameters and Expected/Marginal Moments — get_expected_Sigma_from_S
text:
NIW model \(D\) dimensions, scatter matrix \(S\), degrees freedom / pseudocounts \(
u > D + 1\), expected covariance matrix : $$\Sigma =  rac{S}{
u - D - 1}$$ Conversely, scatter matrix obtained \(\Sigma\) : $$S = \Sigma \cdot (
u - D - 1)$$. conjugate NIW NIX models, expected mean \(\mu\) identically equal location parameter \(m\): $$\mu = m$$

title: Convert Between NIW/NIX Hyperparameters and Expected/Marginal Moments — get_expected_Sigma_from_S
text: Murphy KP (2012). Machine learning: probabilistic perspective. MIT Press.
