title: Plot categorization decision functions and response boundaries — plot_categorization_functions
text: x MVBU object (MVBU_CategoryRepresentation, MVBU_CategoryRepresentationTemplate, MVBU_CognitiveModel, MVBU_Stanfit). cues Character vector cue names plot (1, 2, 3 cues). Defaults cues model 3 (first 3 cues model 3 cues, analytically marginalizing remaining dimensions). 3 cue dimensions can plotted simultaneously. categories Character vector category names evaluate plot. Defaults first category (get_category_labels(x)[1L]). groups Character vector group names plot. Defaults NULL (groups). aes Plot aesthetic: "contour", "fill", "fill-gradient", "fill-discrete". Defaults "contour" 1D/2D static plots, "fill-discrete" 2D interactive plots (interactive = TRUE). interactive = TRUE (aes = "interactive"), renders 3D response probability surface via Plotly. levels Numeric vector specifying response probability contour levels. Defaults c(0.01, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.99). limits Optional named list numeric vector specifying axis / cue limits (e.g. list(F1 = c(200, 800), F2 = c(800, 2500))). Defaults NULL (automatically computed category distributions exemplars). decision_rule Character string specifying decision rule use categorization predictions ("proportional", "criterion", "sampling"). Defaults "proportional". resolution Integer specifying grid resolution along continuous cue dimensions. Defaults 100L 1D 60L 2D/3D. noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise evaluation: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". Defaults NULL (uses model's configured noise treatment). lapse_treatment Optional character string specifying treatment attentional lapses: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; categorization reflects pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs posterior replaced lapse_bias. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many encounters (expected response probabilities), mixing normative posteriors lapse_bias: \((1 - \lambda) p(c \mid x) + \lambda b_c\). Defaults NULL (uses model's configured lapse treatment). ... Additional arguments passed specific plotting methods: uncertainty_treatment: Treatment posterior parameter uncertainty fitted Stan models ("marginalize" "sample"). ndraws: Integer specifying number posterior MCMC draws use MVBU_Stanfit (defaults 20L). show_exposure_data, show_test_data: Logical; TRUE, overlays observed exposure/test data points. parallel, n_cores: Logical integer controlling parallel grid evaluation. noise_treatment: Optional character string specifying perceptual noise treatment ("no_noise", "sample", "marginalize"). interactive: Logical; TRUE, produces interactive 3D WebGL scenes via Plotly. slices, slice_cue: Configuration 3D sliced category plots.

title: Transform and untransform means, covariances, and cognitive models — transform_model
text: Gaussian Normal-Inverse-Wishart distributions transform analytically affine maps \(y = (x + b)\): $$\mu' = (\mu + b), \quad \Sigma' = \Sigma ^T$$

title: Transform and untransform means, covariances, and cognitive models — transform_model
code: df <- data.frame(vot = rnorm(30, 20, 10), f0 = rnorm(30, 220, 25)) trans <- get_affine_transform(df, cues = c("vot", "f0"),                               type = "standardize")  # Transform mean vector and covariance matrix m <- c("vot" = 20, "f0" = 220) S <- matrix(c(100, 20, 20, 625), nrow = 2,             dimnames = list(c("vot", "f0"), c("vot", "f0"))) m_trans <- transform_mean(m, trans) S_trans <- transform_cov(S, trans)  # Untransform back to original space untransform_mean(m_trans, trans) #> vot  f0  #>  20 220  untransform_cov(S_trans, trans) #>     vot  f0 #> vot 100  20 #> f0   20 625  # Transform an entire cognitive model mod <- example_mvg_ideal_observer(n_cues = 2) mod_trans <- transform_model(mod, trans) untransform_model(mod_trans, trans) #> <MVBeliefUpdatr::MVG_IdealObserver> #>   Categories (6): /b/, /d/, /g/, /k/, /p/, /t/ #>   Cues (2): VOT, f0_semitones #>   Decision rule: sampling #>   Category prior: /b/: 0.167, /d/: 0.167, /g/: 0.167, /k/: 0.167, /p/: 0.167, /t/: 0.167 #>   Lapse rate: 0 (treatment: no_lapses) #>   Perceptual noise: none (treatment: no_noise) #>   Category representations (6): #>     /b/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /d/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /g/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /k/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /p/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2)) #>     /t/: MVG(mu = vector(2), Sigma = matrix(2, 2))

title: Update a model's category-representation template from observations — update_template
text: x NIW_IdealAdaptor, NIX_IdealAdaptor, MNIX_IdealAdaptor object. observations data.frame tibble containing cue columns , update_method = "label-certain", category column. updating Either "batch" "incremental". Batch updates currently supported update_method = "label-certain". Default "batch". keep_history TRUE incremental updating, return list intermediate models followed final model. Default FALSE. lapse_treatment Treatment attentional lapses updating label-uncertain models: "no_lapses", "sample", "marginalize". "no_lapses": Lapses ignored; updating reflects pure normative evidence evaluation (even lapse_rate > 0). "sample": Simulates stochastic attentional lapses individual observations. probability lapse_rate, lapse occurs observation treated uninformative updating. "marginalize": Evaluates updating expectation across infinitely many encounters; evidence downweighted \(1 - \lambda\). Default "no_lapses". noise_treatment Treatment perceptual noise categorization label-uncertain updating: "no_noise", "sample", "marginalize". "no_noise": perceptual noise applied input cues, noise assumed categorization. "sample": Simulates sensory noise specific observation. Noise drawn \(\mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_{\text{noise}})\) added input cues (projected composite cue space early integration), observer accounts noise uncertainty categorization adding \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) likelihood scale. "marginalize": Evaluates categorization limit across infinitely many noisy encounters (expected consequences). noise sampled onto input stimulus, \(\Sigma_{\text{noise}}\) added category covariance scale. Default "no_noise". update_method One "-updating", "label-certain", "nolabel-criterion", "nolabel-sampling", "nolabel-proportional", "nolabel-uniform". Default "label-certain". ... title: MVBeliefUpdatr 0.1.0
text: Initial release MVBeliefUpdatr, package modeling, fitting, visualizing incremental Bayesian categorization belief updating Gaussian ideal observers ideal adaptors.

title: MVBeliefUpdatr 0.1.0
text: Unified hierarchy cognitive models based R’s modern ‘S7’ class system. MVBU_CategoryRepresentation: category distribution representations univariate Gaussian (UVG), multivariate Gaussian (MVG), univariate Gaussian category-specific variance (MUVG). MVBU_CategoryTemplate: collections category representations representing observer’s prior updated beliefs. MVBU_CognitiveModel: ideal observers, ideal adaptors, exemplar-based categorization models.

title: MVBeliefUpdatr 0.1.0
text: Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (NIX) 1D cues. Normal-Inverse-Wishart (NIW) multivariate cues. Multivariate Normal-Inverse-Chi-squared (MNIX) multivariate cues diagonal covariance matrices. Unknown prior mean unknown prior variance/covariance (Case 1). Unknown prior mean known prior variance/covariance (Case 2). Known prior mean unknown prior variance/covariance (Case 3). Known prior mean known prior variance/covariance (Case 4). Declarative prior specification parameter_prior(), supporting informative Normal, Cauchy, LKJ, Beta, Dirichlet priors. Partial global parameter fixing fix_parameter().

title: MVBeliefUpdatr 0.1.0
text: Pre-compiled Stan models providing full Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) parameter estimation univariate multivariate Gaussian ideal adaptors. Integration ‘loo’ Leave-One-Cross-Validation model comparison via loo(), waic(), loo_compare(). Tidy extraction methods (get_parameters(), get_draws(), get_predictions()) supporting natural cue space standardized space.
